cells.forex: At a retail broker you usually hold a contract on the rate, not the currencies themselves.
cells.stocks: Bought with your own cash, a share is part-ownership of the company; borrowing to buy changes the risk.
cells.penny_stocks: Also part-ownership, but small companies can issue many new shares, shrinking each holder's slice.
cells.commodities: Most practice-level routes are contracts or funds; owning the physical goods is a different business with storage costs.
cells.futures: A contract to buy or sell later, held on [[margin]]; nothing is owned until settlement, if ever.

caveat: Product type decides this, not the market name. A broker's contract on a share is not the same as owning the share, so read what the product actually is.
